name: FALLEN PRIEST OF THE SLEEPING GOD

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
FALLEN PRIEST OF THE SLEEPING GOD 		
DIFFICULTY 10

Size 1 frightening monster (aquatic)
Perception 13 (+3); darksight
Defense 12; Health 40; Insanity 6, Corruption 4
Strength 11 (+1), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 11 (+1), Will 12 (+2)
Speed 10; swimmer
Amphibious A fallen priest can breathe while submerged in
water.
Sleeper Awakens Before the fallen priest makes an attack roll
or a challenge roll, they can use this trait to roll with 1 boon.
If the roll results in a failure, the priest gains 1 Insanity and
becomes dazed instead of frightened as a result of gaining
Insanity in this way.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Trident (melee or short range) +1 with 1 boon (1d6 or 2d6
with Sleeper Awakens)

SPECIAL ATTACKS
Tentacle Wrench The fallen priest targets one creature
within medium range. A watery tentacle appears in the air,
hardens, and lashes out at the target. Make a Will attack
roll with 1 boon against the target’s Agility. On a success,
the target takes 1d6 damage and moves 5 yards in a
direction the priest chooses.

name: AGENTS OF THE SLEEPER

source.reason: Explicit CUR-003 source reference; edition/permission not certified.

originalText:
Agents of the Sleeper
The cult depends on capable individuals to do the work
of finding the Astronomica, defending the priests and their
temples, and eliminating enemies. Like the priests, these
agents bear markings of their service, corruptions of
the flesh and mind that demonstrate their steady loss of
humanity.

AGENTS OF THE SLEEPER

DIFFICULTY 5

Size 1 monster
Perception 11 (+1)
Defense 14 (brigandine, small shield); Health 15; Insanity 4,
Corruption 2
Strength 12 (+2), Agility 10 (+0), Intellect 10 (+0), Will 11 (+1)
Speed 10
Gift of the Sleeping God Before the agent makes an attack
roll or challenge roll, they can use this trait to make the roll
with a number of boons equal to their Insanity. If the roll
results in a failure, the agent gains 1 Insanity and becomes
stunned until the end of their next turn.

ATTACK OPTIONS
Saber (melee) +2 with 1 boon (1d6 + 2)
Crab Claw (melee) +2 with 1 boon (1d6 plus grab)
Grab As part of the attack, the agent can attempt to
grab the target. The agent can maintain a grab using a
triggered action on their turn.

--- PDF p. 5 ---
The Astronomica
The Cult of the New God understood the peril the
Astronomica posed and thus moved to remove it from the
lands of the Empire. Dozens of incomplete copies, partially
transcribed from an authentic copy, went into the pyres,
as did several fabrications, books bearing the title but
filled with nonsense. The Cult managed to secure several
authentic, complete books and then burned them. One
copy, however, escaped their clutches: the original.
The Astromica’s size and bulk make concealing it difficult:
It weighs 30 pounds and measures 3 feet by 2 feet by 1
foot. Worse, anyone lugging it around feels as if some
liquid sloshes around inside, which makes it even more
cumbersome. Some kind of coral-like growth completely
covers the book, even the pages. A starfish is found on one
side. Twisting it to the right detaches it from the book’s
surface. Once free, a potential reader must place the
starfish over their face, at which point it becomes affixed
until removed. Removing it deals 1 damage as the starfish
grows quite comfortable and loses interest in independent
living. While the starfish is in place, the reader sees the
book open—no others do—to reveal a pool of water. Words
swim up in the pool and disappear when read. It takes 80
hours to read the book, and only by finishing it can one
gain its powers.
Dread Knowledge of the Sleeping God: You gain 1d3
Insanity, 3 Corruption, and you become cursed (as if by
a rank 7 spell). While cursed in this way, you become
impaired while you are not submerged in water.
Magical Secrets: You discover the Madness and Water
traditions if you have not discovered them already. If
you have, you learn a rank 0 spell from the tradition
instead. Details on the Madness tradition appear in
Occult Philosophy.
Awaken the Sleeping God: The book contains a ritual
to awaken the sleeping one. The ritual requires 100
gc worth of exotic ingredients, the participation of 8
people, and 24 hours of constant prayer and recitals
of the mystic words, all performed on the edge of
the Auroral Ocean. Upon finishing the ritual, each
participant takes 8d6 damage and gains Insanity equal
to their Will scores. Then, the seas froth as a demon
prince rises from the depths. (See The Hunger in the
Void, page 64, for rules.) The prince looks exactly like
the idol: a towering humanoid with a squid head and
a mass of writhing tentacles surrounding its beak. The
now awakened thing rampages across the countryside,
visiting death and destruction to everything in its path.

5

A Dark Tide Rises
The Seekers of the Sleeping God present a grave danger
to Rûl. They act to awaken their eldritch master, heedless
of the horrors doing so will unleash on the world. The
Sleeping God’s influence blinds them to the reality of
what their service will bring and to the ravages that
worshipping their master inflicts upon their flesh. You can
use the following campaign structure to create a series of
adventures featuring the cult. Each tier includes a Shadow
of the Demon Lord to describe the perilous conditions
brought on by the Hunger’s attention.

Stirrings in the Deep (Novice)
The orcs invade the Holy Kingdom. They butcher the
inhabitants, torture the priests, and sack the temples. A
strange group of people follow them, seemingly priests of
Oceanus. However the characters become involved, they
must contend with the priests who take some acolytes
prisoner and torture them for information concerning a
lost tome they call the Astronomica.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: Gray-green clouds blot out
the skies and remain. Sometimes, they swirl around.
One can see emerald lightning reach down to scorch the
earth. It rains two days out of every three.

Seaward Shenanigans (Expert)
After a merchant ship loaded with medical supplies never
reaches Freeport, the authorities hire the player characters
to find it and recover what they can. During the voyage, the
characters encounter storms, a kraken attack, and devotees
of a bizarre god peering into the deep to find their sleeping
master. The characters learn that the cultists attack ships
and take them to widen the range of their search.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: It now rains every day and
flooding becomes a problem. Worse, the raindrops
contain some slimy mucus that taints water. People who
drink the tainted water gain fishy mutations after 1d3
days.

The Dread Ritual (Master)
The cultists recover the Astronomica and locate the Sleeping
One. They gather to perform the ritual on a ship when
Tarterus hides from the night sky, and all the planets align
with Urth in a row. The characters learn about the attempt
and have 24 hours to stop the ritual before it finishes. The
group must track down the ship, deal with the various
guardians in their path, and thwart Kristane and the
demons he summons, or all is lost.
Shadow of the Demon Lord: The rains become
downpours. Sea levels rise, and most coastal cities
and settlements drown. Worse, mutated people run
amok through the countryside, screeching and hooting
prayers to the Sleeper.
